subject: social_science
chapter_title: Banks and the Magic of Finance

concepts.title: Why Banks Matter
concepts.definition: Banks keep the community's money safe and put it to work: they accept deposits, lend to businesses and families, and thus turn idle savings into productive credit, as Schumpeter's words on the banker suggest.
concepts.key_idea: A bank is a bridge between savers and borrowers: both sides gain, and ideas get funded.

concepts.title: Types of Bank Accounts
concepts.definition: Banks offer different accounts for different needs: a savings account for storing money with interest, a current account for business with many transactions, and fixed deposit accounts that lock money for a term at a higher rate.
concepts.key_idea: Match the account to the purpose: daily convenience, safe saving or locked growth.

concepts.title: Interest and the Magic of Compounding
concepts.definition: Interest is payment for the use of money; with compounding, interest is paid on interest too, so a deposit of 1000 at 6 percent a year grows to 1060 in one year and about 2012 in twelve years.
concepts.key_idea: Compounding rewards patience: money grows slowly at first, then faster every year, like a snowball.

concepts.title: Loans and the Discipline of Credit
concepts.definition: Banks lend depositors' money as loans for homes, studies, farm and business; credit must be used with discipline, since every loan must be repaid with interest, and default harms both borrower and bank.
concepts.key_idea: Credit is a tool with two edges: wise loans create income that repays them, reckless ones bury households in debt.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the same Rs 1000 stays deposited at 6% for 12 years, what amount does it grow to?

solution_template.action: turn the rate into a fraction
